title.source: Section check: Civics, Media & Everyday Economics
title.back: Section review: Citizens, media and everyday economics

intro.source: 10 questions about Lessons 20–24. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 10 questions about Lessons 20-24. Take your time. You can look at the lessons again and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.note: 'Điều cần thiết' for need and 'điều muốn có' for want: my choice (KEY_TERMS has no entry). Alternatives: 'nhu cầu' / 'mong muốn'. Check the Vietnamese Lesson 20 uses the same.
questions.0.question.source: Which of these is a need, not a want?
questions.0.question.back: Which of these is a need, not a want?

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Music videos are nice, but you can live without them. That makes them a want. Look back at Lesson 20.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Music videos are fun, but you can still live without them. So they are a want. Look at Lesson 20 again.

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A new football is fun, but you can live without it. That makes it a want. Look back at Lesson 20.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A new football is fun, but you can still live without it. So it is a want. Look at Lesson 20 again.

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. You must have clean water to live and stay healthy. That makes it a need.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. You must have clean water to live and stay healthy. So it is a need.

questions.1.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks.

questions.1.stimulus.body.note: Amani is an invented name, kept. 'Trung tâm học tập' for learning centre. 'Máy tính bảng' for tablet.
questions.1.stimulus.body.source: Amani and two friends share one tablet at a made-up learning centre. They have 30 minutes left on it today. They can play a word game or watch a short science video. There is not enough time for both. They choose the science video.
questions.1.stimulus.body.back: Amani and two friends share one tablet at a made-up learning centre. Today they have 30 minutes left to use it. They can play a word game or watch a short science video. There is not enough time for both. They choose the science video.

questions.1.question.note: 'Chi phí cơ hội' for opportunity cost is the standard economics term but may be hard for a 12-year-old; check the Lesson 20 glossary explains it in the same words.
questions.1.question.source: What is the opportunity cost of their choice?
questions.1.question.back: What is the opportunity cost of that choice?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: The word game they do not play
questions.1.options.0.text.back: The word game they did not play

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The word game is the next-best thing they give up. That is their opportunity cost.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. The word game is the next best thing they give up. That is their opportunity cost.

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The video is what they choose. The opportunity cost is what they give up. Look back at Lesson 20.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The video is what they choose. The opportunity cost is what they give up. Look at Lesson 20 again.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: The tablet that they all share

questions.1.options.2.feedback.note: 'Tài nguyên' for 'resource' follows KEY_TERMS but sounds odd for a tablet; reviewer may prefer 'nguồn lực' or 'thứ họ có để dùng'.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The tablet is a resource they use. The opportunity cost is the thing they give up. Look back at Lesson 20.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The tablet is a resource they use. The opportunity cost is what they give up. Look at Lesson 20 again.

questions.2.question.note: Jun and Lucia are invented names, kept. 'Đổi chác' for 'barter': my choice (alternatives: 'hàng đổi hàng', 'trao đổi trực tiếp'). 'Sự khan hiếm' for scarcity. 'Ngân sách' for budget: may be stiff; alternative 'kế hoạch chi tiêu' for money. Please decide.
questions.2.question.source: Here is a made-up example. Jun fixes a broken chair for Lucia. In return, Lucia teaches Jun a card game. No money is used. What is this kind of exchange called?
questions.2.question.back: This is a made-up example. Jun fixes Lucia's broken chair. In return, Lucia teaches Jun a card game. Nobody uses money. What is this kind of exchange called?

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Scarcity means there is not enough for every use. Here, two people swap skills with no money. Look back at Lesson 21.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Scarcity means not enough for everything needed. Here, two people swap skills without using money. Look at Lesson 21 again.

questions.2.options.1.text.note: Review: Lesson 21 glossary term for barter is 'hàng đổi hàng' (14 uses, 'đổi chác' never). Feedback now also says swapping for something else. [Reviewer changed: Đổi chác → Hàng đổi hàng (and feedback sentence)]

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Barter means swapping a thing or a skill without using money. Jun and Lucia swap skills.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. Swapping means exchanging one thing or skill without using money. Jun and Lucia swap skills.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A budget is a plan for money or time. Here, two people swap skills with no money. Look back at Lesson 21.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A budget is a plan for money or time. Here, two people swap skills without using money. Look at Lesson 21 again.

questions.3.question.note: 'Lòng tin' for trust (KEY_TERMS). 'Lừa gạt' for 'cheats'. Check it is not too strong.
questions.3.question.source: Lesson 21 says every exchange depends on trust. What happens when a seller cheats?
questions.3.question.back: Lesson 21 says every exchange depends on trust. What happens when a seller cheats?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: More people want to buy from them.
questions.3.options.0.text.back: More people want to buy from them.

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. People do not want to buy from someone who cheats. Look back at Lesson 21.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. People do not want to buy from a cheat. Look at Lesson 21 again.

questions.3.options.1.text.back: People no longer trust the seller.

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. If someone cheats, people stop trusting them. Then trade gets harder for everyone.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. If someone cheats, people no longer trust them. Then trading becomes harder for everyone.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: Nothing changes at the market at all.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Cheating breaks trust, and then trade gets harder for everyone. Look back at Lesson 21.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Cheating loses trust, and then trading becomes harder for everyone. Look at Lesson 21 again.

questions.4.question.note: Mei is an invented name, kept. 'Ngân sách thời gian' idea expressed as 'Kế hoạch thời gian' in the question and 'ngân sách' in the options; check the link is clear to the learner. | Review: English 'time budget'; options and lesson 22 use ngân sách (thời gian). [Reviewer changed: Kế hoạch thời gian của Mei → Ngân sách thời gian của Mei]
questions.4.question.source: Mei's time budget has 15 minutes for reading English and 15 minutes for games on the shared phone. What does this show?
questions.4.question.back: Mei's time plan has 15 minutes to read English and 15 minutes to play a game on the shared phone. What does this show?

questions.4.options.0.text.note: A budget for time, not only money: check 'ngân sách' for time is natural; alternative 'kế hoạch'. | Review: Correct option is the longest (same in English).
questions.4.options.0.text.source: A budget can plan time, not only money.
questions.4.options.0.text.back: A budget can plan time, not only money.

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Budgets are not only for money. Mei uses a budget to plan her time in the evening.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. A budget is not only for money. Mei uses a budget to plan her evening time.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: A budget means Mei can never play games.
questions.4.options.1.text.back: Having a budget means Mei can never play games.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Mei still has 15 minutes for games. She just has less time for them. Look back at Lesson 22.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Mei still has 15 minutes to play games. She just has less time for it. Look at Lesson 22 again.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: A budget is only ever a plan for money.
questions.4.options.2.text.back: A budget is always only a plan for money.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Mei's budget is a plan for her time. Budgets are not only for money. Look back at Lesson 22.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Mei's budget is a plan for her time. A budget is not only for money. Look at Lesson 22 again.

questions.5.question.note: 'Mục tiêu nhỏ, ngắn hạn' for 'small, short goals'. Check.
questions.5.question.source: Lesson 22 says that small, short goals are useful. Why?
questions.5.question.back: Lesson 22 says small, short-term goals are useful. Why?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: They do not need any steps or plan.
questions.5.options.0.text.back: They need no steps or plan.

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. You still work towards a goal step by step. Look back at Lesson 22.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. You still have to move toward the goal step by step. Look at Lesson 22 again.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: They make sure nothing will ever change.
questions.5.options.1.text.back: They guarantee that nothing will change.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Plans can still change. That is why a small goal you can work on now helps. Look back at Lesson 22.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Plans can still change. So a small goal you can do now is useful. Look at Lesson 22 again.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: You can start to work on them now.
questions.5.options.2.text.back: You can start doing them right now.

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Plans can change, but you can work on a small goal now. One example is learning 10 new words a week.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. Plans can change, but you can do a small goal right now. One example is learning 10 new words each week.

questions.6.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks.
questions.6.stimulus.title.source: Message F, a made-up message from Lesson 23
questions.6.stimulus.title.back: Message F, a made-up message in Lesson 23

questions.6.stimulus.items.0.source: A photo of a fish as long as a bus.
questions.6.stimulus.items.0.back: A photo of a fish as long as a bus.

questions.6.stimulus.items.1.note: Lakeside is an invented place, kept as it is.
questions.6.stimulus.items.1.source: The words say: “Caught at Lakeside yesterday.”
questions.6.stimulus.items.1.back: The text says: "Caught at Lakeside yesterday."

questions.6.stimulus.items.2.source: The edges of the fish look strange.
questions.6.stimulus.items.2.back: The edge of the fish looks strange.

questions.6.stimulus.items.3.source: Nobody else has a photo of this fish.
questions.6.stimulus.items.3.back: Nobody else has a photo of this fish.

questions.6.question.note: Media-literacy lesson (23). Check 'có thể không thật' is clear and not frightening.
questions.6.question.source: Which detail is a clue that the photo may not be real?
questions.6.question.back: Which detail is a clue that the photo may not be real?

questions.6.options.0.text.source: It is a photo, not a written message.
questions.6.options.0.text.back: It is a photo, not a written message.

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A photo can be real or changed. Being a photo does not show it is fake. Look back at Lesson 23.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A photo can be real or edited. Being a photo does not show it is fake. Look at Lesson 23 again.

questions.6.options.1.text.source: The edges of the fish look strange.
questions.6.options.1.text.back: The edge of the fish looks strange.

questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Strange edges can show that a photo was changed with an app. Also, nobody else has a photo of this fish.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. A strange edge can show the photo was edited with an app. Also, nobody else has a photo of this fish.

questions.6.options.2.text.source: It says where the fish was caught.
questions.6.options.2.text.back: It says where the fish was caught.

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Naming a place does not show a photo is fake. Think about how the fish itself looks. Look back at Lesson 23.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Naming a place does not show the photo is fake. Think about what the fish itself looks like. Look at Lesson 23 again.

questions.7.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks.

questions.7.stimulus.body.note: Pia is an invented name, kept. 'City Park' translated as 'Công viên Thành phố' (invented name): reviewer may prefer to keep 'City Park'. 'Nhóm trò chuyện' for group chat.
questions.7.stimulus.body.source: Pia plays in a football team. She sees a message in a group chat. It says: “Our match at City Park is now on Sunday. Tell the whole team.” The message has no name and no date. Pia does not know who wrote it.
questions.7.stimulus.body.back: Pia plays on a football team. She sees a message in the group chat. The message says: "Our match at City Park is now moved to Sunday. Tell the whole team." The message has no name and no date. Pia does not know who wrote it.

questions.7.question.source: What is the best thing for Pia to do first?
questions.7.question.back: What is the best thing Pia should do first?

questions.7.options.0.text.source: Send it to the whole team right now
questions.7.options.0.text.back: Send it to the whole team right away

questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The message has no name or date, so Pia cannot trust it yet. It is safer to check first. Look back at Lesson 23.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The message has no name or date, so Pia cannot trust it yet. Checking first is safer. Look at Lesson 23 again.

questions.7.options.1.text.source: Believe it, because it sounds very sure
questions.7.options.1.text.back: Believe it right away, because it sounds very sure

questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A message can sound sure and still be wrong. Pia needs to check it first. Look back at Lesson 23.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A message can sound very sure and still be wrong. Pia needs to check first. Look at Lesson 23 again.

questions.7.options.2.text.source: Ask her coach if the message is true
questions.7.options.2.text.back: Ask the coach whether it is correct

questions.7.options.2.feedback.note: 'Kiểm chứng' for verify (KEY_TERMS, alternative 'xác minh'); 'nguồn đáng tin' for trusted source.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Her coach is a trusted source. Pia can verify the message before she shares it.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. The coach is a trustworthy source. Pia can verify the message before sharing.

questions.8.question.note: 'Bên liên quan' for stakeholder per KEY_TERMS; hard for young readers, check the feedback explains it.
questions.8.question.source: Lesson 24 says the bus users are stakeholders. What does that word mean?
questions.8.question.back: Lesson 24 says bus riders are stakeholders. What does that word mean?

questions.8.options.0.text.source: A person or group that a problem affects
questions.8.options.0.text.back: A person or group affected by a problem

questions.8.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The litter at the bus stop affects the bus users and the centre manager. So they are stakeholders.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. Rubbish at the bus stop affects bus riders and the centre's manager. So they are stakeholders.

questions.8.options.1.text.source: A person who sells goods at a market stall
questions.8.options.1.text.back: A person selling goods at a market stall

questions.8.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The bus users are not selling anything. A stakeholder is someone a problem or plan affects. Look back at Lesson 24.
questions.8.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Bus riders do not sell anything. A stakeholder is a person a problem or plan affects. Look at Lesson 24 again.

questions.8.options.2.text.source: A person who checks if a message is true
questions.8.options.2.text.back: A person who checks whether a message is true

questions.8.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Checking messages is part of Lesson 23. A stakeholder is someone a problem or plan affects. Look back at Lesson 24.
questions.8.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Checking messages belongs to Lesson 23. A stakeholder is a person a problem or plan affects. Look at Lesson 24 again.

questions.9.question.source: What does Lesson 24 say about ways to help a community?
questions.9.question.back: What does Lesson 24 say about ways to help a community?

questions.9.options.0.text.source: Small, everyday actions can make a difference.
questions.9.options.0.text.back: Small everyday actions can make a difference.

questions.9.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Reading with a younger child or keeping a shared room clean can help a community.
questions.9.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. Reading with a small child or keeping a shared room clean can help a community.

questions.9.options.1.text.source: Only big campaigns can make a real difference.
questions.9.options.1.text.back: Only big campaigns make a real difference.

questions.9.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Helping does not have to mean a big campaign. Everyday actions matter too. Look back at Lesson 24.
questions.9.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Helping does not have to be a big campaign. Everyday actions also matter. Look at Lesson 24 again.

questions.9.options.2.text.source: You must speak in public to help at all.
questions.9.options.2.text.back: You must speak in front of a crowd to help.

questions.9.options.2.feedback.note: The English says you never need to 'take risks'; rendered 'làm điều mạo hiểm'. Sensitive for displaced youth: please check it is tactful.
questions.9.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. You never need to speak in public, post online or take risks to help. Look back at Lesson 24.
questions.9.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. You never need to speak in front of a crowd, post online or do anything risky to help. Look at Lesson 24 again.

results.high.note: Check 'cách đưa ra lựa chọn, kiểm tra tin nhắn và giúp đỡ một cộng đồng' is natural.
results.high.source: Well done. You know a lot about making choices, checking messages and helping a community.
results.high.back: Well done. You know a lot about making choices, checking messages and helping a community.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good. You answered many correctly. Look at the lessons again for the ones not right, and try again if you like.
results.middle.note: Review: Unnatural preposition. [Reviewer changed: cho những câu chưa đúng → về những câu bạn chưa làm đúng]

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 20–24, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Look at Lessons 20-24 again then try again. You can take as much time as you like.
